title: Modeling and numerical simulations of dendritic crystal growth
one_sentence_summary: Kobayashi couples an anisotropic non-conserved phase field to latent-heat diffusion and shows qualitatively that interfacial anisotropy, dimensionless latent heat, and interface-localized noise reorganize dendrite tips, branches, screening, and corner formation without explicit front tracking.

study_identity.domain: Anisotropic phase-field simulation of pure-melt dendritic solidification
study_identity.evidence_mode: Free-energy formulation, sharp-interface asymptotics, and qualitative two-dimensional parameter studies

module_alignment.module_title: CVD-deposited nanosilicon in micron-scale porous carbon
module_alignment.rationale: The paper contains neither silicon, carbon pores, chemical vapor deposition, nor battery electrochemistry; only its generic diffuse-interface numerics could be reused.

module_alignment.module_title: Phase transformation, crystallization, and mechanical conditions in lithiated silicon
module_alignment.rationale: It treats liquid-solid crystallization and interfacial anisotropy, but excludes mechanics and has no lithium-bearing phase or mechanically controlled crystallization criterion.

It is a foundational phase-field example for moving interfaces, free energy, anisotropy, and diffusion coupling, but it contains thermal rather than electrochemical transport and no force balance or constitutive mechanics.
The sharp-interface limit links diffuse-interface and interfacial descriptions, yet there is no atomistic parameterization, scale-by-scale property transfer, system model, or experimental closure.

one_sentence_conclusion.text: A minimal anisotropic phase-field/temperature model can reproduce a wide range of dendritic morphologies qualitatively, but its quantitative fidelity is limited by diffuse-interface thickness and the available spatial and temporal resolution.

why_worth_reading.text: This is a compact foundational case showing how free energy, angular interface anisotropy, latent-heat coupling, sharp-interface interpretation, perturbations, and numerical resolution jointly determine emergent branching morphology.

research_problem.text: The work asks for the smallest whole-domain field model that can handle changing solid-liquid topology and generate realistic dendritic patterns without explicitly storing and moving the interface.

prior_gap.text: Explicit moving-boundary methods require difficult interface bookkeeping when fronts merge or detach and are hard to extend to three dimensions; existing isotropic phase-field models do not by themselves explain strongly oriented dendrites.

core_contribution.text: The paper formulates an orientation-dependent Allen-Cahn-type phase field coupled to an enthalpy heat equation, relates it asymptotically to an anisotropic curvature law, and maps morphology changes against latent heat, anisotropy mode and strength, and noise.

scope_boundary.text: The model is for pure one-component melt growth with equal thermal diffusivity in solid and liquid; it omits fluid flow, transformation mechanics, solute transport, electrochemical reactions, and quantitative convergence, and its snowflake-like patterns are not vapor-growth snowflakes.

research_object.text: A pure one-component melt solidifies into a crystal whose solid-liquid boundary can become cellular or dendritic under thermal driving.

geometry_and_scale.text: All reported calculations are two-dimensional, using either a 9×9 square domain or a 12×3 rectangular channel with a diffuse interface of characteristic thickness controlled by epsilon.

phases_and_composition.text: The order parameter p equals 0 in liquid and 1 in solid; the steep transition between them is the interface. There is no composition field because the modeled material is a pure melt.

process_and_loading.text: Thermal undercooling drives solidification, heat diffusion removes or redistributes latent heat, interfacial energy smooths curvature, anisotropy selects preferred directions, and small random perturbations seed side branches.

state_variables.text: The solved fields are phase p(r,t) and nondimensional temperature T(r,t); interface orientation theta, normal velocity V, curvature kappa, and capillary function d0(theta) are derived quantities.

target_outputs.text: The calculations target crystal-interface morphology, dendrite-tip and side-branch evolution, branch competition and screening, corner formation, and their qualitative dependence on K, delta, j, and noise amplitude.

framework.text: A non-conserved Ginzburg-Landau phase field with orientation-dependent gradient energy is coupled bidirectionally to a heat-diffusion equation through temperature-dependent driving and latent-heat release.

assumptions.text: The material is a pure melt and one thermal diffusion field limits growth; convection, Marangoni flow, and transformation expansion or shrinkage are neglected.
Thermal diffusivity is identical in solid and liquid, and the bulk phase minima remain fixed at p=0 and p=1 so latent heat is released only where the interface passes.
The diffuse interface is thin relative to resolved morphology, while stochastic forcing is localized by p(1-p) and therefore acts mainly near the interface.

free_energy.text: The Ginzburg-Landau functional combines a gradient penalty with a quartic double-well potential whose stable minima are liquid p=0 and solid p=1.
The potential-depth difference is proportional to m, so m supplies thermodynamic phase preference; orientation dependence in epsilon converts interfacial energy into anisotropic capillarity.

governing_equations.label: Ginzburg-Landau free energy
governing_equations.explanation: The gradient term assigns a finite cost and thickness to the interface, while the double well stabilizes bulk liquid and solid states and biases one phase through m.

governing_equations.label: Anisotropic phase-field evolution
governing_equations.latex: \tau\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}=-\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(\epsilon\epsilon'\frac{\partial p}{\partial y})+\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(\epsilon\epsilon'\frac{\partial p}{\partial x})+\nabla\cdot(\epsilon^2\nabla p)+p(1-p)(p-\frac12+m)
governing_equations.explanation: Variational relaxation moves the diffuse interface; angular derivatives of epsilon add anisotropic capillarity, diffusion regularizes the interface, and the local polynomial supplies phase conversion and thermal driving.

governing_equations.label: Latent-heat diffusion
governing_equations.explanation: Temperature diffuses and receives a source only where p changes; K measures latent heat relative to cooling strength and couples interface motion back to the thermal field.

governing_equations.label: Sharp-interface interpretation
governing_equations.explanation: In the thin-interface limit, normal velocity balances thermodynamic driving f against orientation-dependent capillary resistance d0 kappa, linking the diffuse model to a moving-boundary law.

constitutive_relations.label: Temperature-dependent driving
constitutive_relations.explanation: Supercooling increases the solidification drive while the arctangent keeps |m| below one half.

constitutive_relations.label: Angular anisotropy
constitutive_relations.explanation: Delta sets anisotropy strength, j sets rotational mode, and theta0 rotates the preferred growth directions.

coupling_logic.text: Temperature controls m(T), which biases phase conversion; changing p releases latent heat through K partial-t p, which changes T and closes the thermal feedback loop.
Interface orientation controls epsilon and capillarity, thereby selecting branch directions, while curvature smooths small features and noise breaks symmetry among competing branches.

parameters.name: Square domain
parameters.role: Domain for centered or wall-driven solidification cases.

parameters.name: Rectangular domain
parameters.role: Channel for directional-solidification cases.

parameters.name: Square mesh
parameters.role: Spatial resolution for square cases.

parameters.name: Rectangular mesh
parameters.role: Spatial resolution for channel cases.

parameters.name: Mean interface thickness
parameters.role: Controls diffuse-interface thickness and approximation to the sharp front.

parameters.name: Phase relaxation time
parameters.role: Controls phase-field kinetic response and explicit stability demand.

parameters.name: Driving saturation
parameters.role: Bounds the temperature-dependent phase driving.

parameters.name: Driving slope
parameters.role: Controls sensitivity of m(T) near equilibrium.

parameters.name: Noise amplitude
parameters.role: Seeds interface perturbations in the baseline simulations.

parameters.name: Time step
parameters.role: Time mesh used for the explicit phase and implicit heat updates.

initial_conditions.text: Cases include equilibrium-temperature liquid cooled from walls, uniformly supercooled liquid with a prescribed nucleus, or a perturbed planar solid-liquid front; the exact case-dependent setup is described alongside each figure.

boundary_conditions.text: The phase field always uses zero normal flux. Thermal boundaries vary by case: cooled walls, a cooled left wall with other walls insulated, or fully adiabatic boundaries for supercooled solidification.

numerical_implementation.text: Equation (3) is advanced with a simple explicit scheme and the heat equation with a simple implicit scheme on uniform two-dimensional meshes; no special interface-tracking technique is used.
Uniform random noise X in [−1/2,1/2] enters as a p(1−p)X, localizing perturbations around the diffuse interface.

reproducibility_check.text: The paper reports governing equations, main parameters, mesh sizes, time step, boundary-condition families, and temporal schemes, so representative qualitative cases can be rebuilt.

Exact update stencils, linear-solver details, stopping criteria, random seeds, initial nuclei for every panel, and original code are absent; the author also states that the reported resolution is not quantitatively converged for interface velocity.

key_results.text: Increasing four-fold anisotropy from zero to 0.050 reorganizes growth from isotropic finger splitting to oriented dendrites with increasingly strong branch screening and preferred directions.
Increasing K destabilizes planar or compact fronts and produces cells, slits, tip splitting, and progressively thinner branching patterns in the sampled thermal regimes.
Noise amplitude strongly changes side-branch selection for non-oscillating tips, whereas oscillatory tip growth makes branching less noise-sensitive.

validation_and_comparison.text: Validation is primarily qualitative: simulated shapes resemble familiar dendrites and reproduce expected smoothing, instability, preferred-direction, screening, and side-branch phenomena.

The asymptotic sharp-interface law provides theoretical consistency between the diffuse equation and thermodynamic driving plus anisotropic curvature, but no grid-converged velocity comparison is reported.
No direct fit to a named material experiment, measured tip velocity, branch spacing, or thermal history is provided.

mechanistic_interpretation.text: Anisotropic capillary derivatives magnify even small angular modulation, selecting branch orientation and permitting corners when d0(theta) becomes negative.
Latent heat reduces local supercooling and couples neighboring tips through the temperature field, creating competition and screening for access to cooling.
Noise does not set the main-tip velocity in the non-oscillating case but biases which young side branches survive competition; a deterministic tip oscillation can instead dominate branch production.

sensitivity_and_uncovered.text: The study varies K, anisotropy strength delta, anisotropy mode j, and noise amplitude, but explores only a small parameter subset and does not provide systematic convergence or uncertainty analysis.
Uncovered physics include convection, mechanical stress and deformation, solute or charge transport, electrochemical interfacial kinetics, multiphase composite boundaries, and vapor-growth facets.

experimental_correspondence.text: The correspondence is morphological rather than quantitative: the simulations generate visually realistic dendrite classes, but they are not calibrated against a specific material specimen or measured field.
Snowflake-like six-fold patterns are explicitly bounded to supercooled-water solidification and cannot be interpreted as validation for vapor-grown snow crystals.

module_value.text: For porous-carbon CVD silicon, this paper supplies only generic moving-interface numerics; it does not inform deposition chemistry, porous architecture, silicon-carbon contact, or battery performance.

For lithiated-silicon phase mechanics, the angular interfacial-energy treatment may inspire crystalline anisotropy models, but lithium thermodynamics, stress, plasticity, and crystallization criteria must be added independently.

For phase-field–mechanics–electrochemistry, the paper is valuable as a clean template for order parameter, double-well free energy, diffuse interface, transport coupling, boundary conditions, anisotropy, perturbations, and resolution limits; thermal coupling must be replaced or extended with electrochemical and mechanical fields.
For multiscale simulation, the diffuse-to-sharp-interface asymptotics demonstrate one cross-description link, but no bottom-up parameter transfer or system-level experimental closure is present.

reusable_elements.text: Reusable elements include the quartic double well, orientation-dependent gradient coefficient, bounded temperature driving, latent-heat source, sharp-interface capillary interpretation, interface-localized noise, and morphology-based parameter studies.
The explicit author warning that interface width must remain below the morphology scale is directly reusable as a mesh and model-resolution acceptance criterion.

limitations_and_next_steps.text: For battery applications, replace temperature-only driving with concentration and electrochemical potential, add stress-dependent free energy and mechanical equilibrium, and define reaction and flux conditions at active interfaces.
Use grid/time convergence, thin-interface analysis, calibrated parameters, and direct experimental observables before interpreting velocities or branch spacings quantitatively.

reproducibility_verdict.text: The qualitative benchmark is substantially reconstructable from the printed equations and settings, and a later independent deal.II implementation exists for an isotropic directional-solidification subset; exact reproduction of the 1993 panels is incomplete because original code, seeds, stencils, and full case files are unavailable.

paper_profile.rationale: The paper introduces a phase-field model, connects it to a sharp-interface limit, and applies it to a suite of dendritic-solidification simulations.

gap.text: Explicit front tracking is cumbersome under topology changes, while a minimal diffuse model still needs anisotropy and thermal feedback to produce realistic dendrites.

core_contribution.text: An anisotropic phase-field equation and latent-heat diffusion equation provide a whole-domain model that generates diverse dendritic morphologies and admits a sharp-interface interpretation.

method_logic.text: The double well marks liquid and solid, gradient energy regularizes the interface, temperature biases phase conversion, latent heat feeds back to temperature, angular epsilon selects directions, and localized noise seeds branch competition.

decisive_evidence.text: The anisotropy sweep produces systematic transitions from fingering to strongly oriented dendrites rather than a single selected picture.
Noise sweeps separate main-tip propagation from side-branch selection and distinguish oscillatory from non-oscillatory branching mechanisms.
The sharp-interface limit explains the roles of thermodynamic driving and anisotropic curvature independently of the numerical morphology panels.

limitations.text: The simulations target qualitative whole-crystal morphology and are not spatially or temporally refined enough for precise interface velocity.
The minimal pure-melt model excludes flow, mechanics, multicomponent transport, and material-specific experimental calibration.

future_work.text: Quantitative use requires smaller interface thickness, finer space and time meshes, restricted domains, and material-specific validation.
Transfer to battery phase separation requires electrochemical transport, reaction boundaries, and mechanics beyond the thermal two-field model.

quick_read.text: p=0 and p=1 denote liquid and solid; a finite transition layer replaces explicit interface tracking.
The phase field is non-conserved and thermally driven, while the heat equation contains K partial-t p as an interface-localized latent-heat source.
Orientation-dependent epsilon and its angular derivatives create anisotropic capillarity and preferred dendrite directions.
The numerical study uses simple explicit/implicit updates on 300×300 or 400×100 grids and emphasizes qualitative morphology rather than converged velocity.
Noise biases side-branch survival, but oscillating tips can generate branches through a stronger, less noise-sensitive mechanism.

central_claims.claim: A minimal anisotropic diffuse-interface model can generate varied dendritic patterns without tracking the interface explicitly.
central_claims.evidence_summary: The same coupled equations produce compact, cellular, split-tip, and oriented dendritic forms as K and anisotropy vary.
central_claims.what_it_proves: The model contains sufficient mechanisms for qualitative morphology generation over the tested cases.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove quantitative predictive accuracy for a particular material or converged interface velocity.
central_claims.open_question: Which thin-interface corrections and calibrated parameters are needed for quantitative prediction?

central_claims.claim: Small anisotropy can control macroscopic branch orientation and corner formation.
central_claims.evidence_summary: Figure 7 changes morphology sharply over delta=0–0.050, while the capillary function explains amplification through angular derivatives.
central_claims.what_it_proves: Angular surface-energy structure is a dominant morphology selector in the modeled regime.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: The chosen cosine anisotropy is not calibrated to a particular crystal's measured interfacial energy.
central_claims.open_question: How should sigma(theta) be inferred from atomistic calculations or experiments for battery materials?

central_claims.claim: Noise primarily controls side-branch selection when deterministic tip oscillation is absent.
central_claims.evidence_summary: Changing noise amplitude alters the side-branch region without changing main-tip speed in one regime, but has weaker effect for oscillating tips.
central_claims.what_it_proves: Different branching regimes can have different sensitivity to perturbations.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: The artificial uniform random forcing is not a measured physical fluctuation spectrum.
central_claims.open_question: Which physical heterogeneities should replace ad hoc noise in composite electrodes?

pipeline.text: Initialize p and T for wall cooling, directional growth, or a nucleus in supercooled melt.
Evaluate orientation-dependent epsilon, bounded thermal driving m(T), and interface-localized random perturbation.
Advance the anisotropic phase field explicitly and the latent-heat equation implicitly, enforcing case-specific thermal and zero-flux phase boundaries.
Compare interface morphology across K, delta, j, and noise amplitude and interpret it with the sharp-interface capillary law.

method_understanding.algorithm_pseudocode:
Initialize p, T, geometry, boundaries, and parameters.
For each time step, compute orientation and m(T), add interface-localized noise, update p explicitly, then update T implicitly with latent heat.
Store p contours and compare morphology across parameter cases.

algorithm_steps.action: Initialize the phase and thermal fields for the selected solidification case.
algorithm_steps.inputs: Domain, mesh, nucleus or planar front, initial T, boundary conditions

algorithm_steps.action: Compute anisotropy, thermal driving, and interface-localized perturbation.
algorithm_steps.inputs: p, T, delta, j, theta0, alpha, gamma, random X

algorithm_steps.action: Advance the phase field explicitly and temperature implicitly.
algorithm_steps.inputs: Current fields, tau, epsilon, K, time step

algorithm_steps.action: Record phase contours and compare branch morphology and speed qualitatively.

engineering_derivation_sketch.text: Take a double-well free energy with a gradient cost, let gradient-flow relaxation evolve p, and make the gradient coefficient depend on interface-normal direction. Couple m to undercooling and enforce enthalpy conservation by adding K partial-t p to heat diffusion. Stretch coordinates across a thin interface to recover a normal-velocity law driven by supercooling and opposed by anisotropic curvature.

implementation_details.text: Uniform grids contain 300×300 or 400×100 points, with time step 0.0002; phase evolution is explicit and heat diffusion implicit.
No special front tracker is used, and the original implementation code and random seeds are not published in the inspected sources.

problem_formulation.text: Approximate an anisotropic thermally driven sharp solid-liquid boundary with two smooth whole-domain fields while retaining thermodynamic driving, capillary smoothing, latent heat, topology change, and preferred crystallographic directions.

key_equations.label: Coupled phase and heat evolution
key_equations.explanation: The phase equation moves and shapes the interface; the heat equation transports and returns latent heat, while temperature closes the feedback through m(T).

key_equations.label: Thin-interface velocity law
key_equations.explanation: Normal velocity is the competition between thermodynamic growth drive and anisotropic curvature penalty.

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: Turns the free-energy variation into phase-field motion.
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: The interface moves so the diffuse free energy decreases, except where thermal driving favors solidification.

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: Couples phase conversion to heat release.
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: Where liquid becomes solid, latent heat locally raises temperature and reduces the remaining undercooling.

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: Connects the whole-domain phase equation to a moving-boundary curvature law.
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: Across a sufficiently thin layer, the diffuse front behaves like an interface with orientation-dependent tension and mobility.

assumptions.text: Pure-melt thermal diffusion is the only rate-limiting bulk field and diffusivity is equal in both phases.
The resolved features are wider than the phase-field layer and numerical meshes are fine enough to suppress lattice-induced anisotropy.

key_results.text: The anisotropic diffuse model reproduces multiple dendrite classes and has a sharp-interface interpretation containing driving, surface tension, and anisotropy.

engineering_proof_sketch.text: Scale interface thickness to zero, introduce a stretched coordinate normal to the front, assume a traveling profile, and solve the resulting nonlinear eigenvalue problem. The leading-order balance yields a velocity proportional to driving minus anisotropic capillary curvature.

limitations.text: The asymptotic connection does not compensate for an interface that is too thick relative to morphology or a grid/time step too coarse for velocity convergence.

task_context.text: The application is qualitative two-dimensional morphology prediction for wall-cooled, directionally solidified, and nucleated pure melts.

experimental_setup.text: There is no laboratory experiment; numerical cases vary latent heat, anisotropy, and perturbation amplitude and compare resulting contour sequences.

constraints.text: Results depend on nondimensional parameters, uniform grids, simplified thermal physics, and diffuse-interface resolution.

transfer_limits.text: Battery use requires replacing pure-melt thermal assumptions with electrochemical free energy, conserved species transport, reaction kinetics, composite geometry, and mechanics; morphology trends cannot be transferred quantitatively as-is.

datasets.text: No dataset is released; evaluation consists of simulated phase-contour sequences across thermal, anisotropy, and noise parameter cases.

metrics.text: The paper mainly evaluates morphology qualitatively: interface stability, cells, tip splitting, branch direction, screening, corners, side-branch region, and approximate tip-velocity behavior.

main_results.text: Anisotropy and latent heat systematically reorganize global dendrite morphology, while noise mainly selects side branches in the non-oscillating regime.

ablation_or_comparison_takeaways.text: The isotropic-to-anisotropic sweep isolates angular interfacial energy as a morphology selector; the noise-amplitude sweep separates stochastic selection from oscillatory branch generation.

numeric_results.interpretation: Small angular modulation is sufficient to move the solution between qualitatively distinct branching regimes.
numeric_results.what_it_does_not_prove: The sweep does not establish a universally optimal anisotropy or a calibrated value for a real material.

numeric_results.interpretation: This is the reported update interval for the qualitative morphology calculations.
numeric_results.what_it_does_not_prove: The paper explicitly does not demonstrate time-step convergence or precise interface velocity.

visual_cards.label: Figures 1-2
visual_cards.source_caption: Diffuse phase-field representation of a solid-liquid interface and the m-controlled double-well potential.
visual_cards.reading_note: Read the steep p transition as the replacement for an explicitly tracked front, then compare how m tilts the two phase minima.

visual_cards.label: Figure 7
visual_cards.source_caption: Four-fold dendrite growth for delta from 0 to 0.050 at K=2.0.
visual_cards.reading_note: Compare rows rather than individual frames: increasing anisotropy converts distributed fingering into strongly oriented trunks and branches.

visual_cards.label: Figures 10-11
visual_cards.source_caption: Noise-amplitude comparison and angular anisotropy/capillary functions.
visual_cards.reading_note: The lower morphology row separates noise-sensitive side branching, while the upper angular plots explain when anisotropic capillarity permits corners.

visual_cards.label: Discussion and Appendix
visual_cards.source_caption: Resolution limitations and thin-interface asymptotic derivation.
visual_cards.reading_note: The left column is essential: the author states that sub-interface features are lost and the reported mesh is not intended for precise velocity.

code.evidence: The accessible implementation is a later deal.II benchmark derived from Kobayashi's formulation; the publication page itself does not expose the program used to generate the 1993 figures.
code.notes: Treat the deal.II example as a reproducible derivative benchmark, not as the original simulation source.

data.evidence: The article reports generated morphology panels rather than a released dataset, and the official record does not identify a data deposit.
data.notes: Figure sequences can be digitized only approximately; original field arrays were not verified.

models.evidence: The mathematical model is fully described in print, but no original executable model or archived case files were verified.
models.notes: The independent deal.II implementation covers only a subset and is listed under code availability.

parser_limitations: The scanned two-column PDF parser assigns most paragraphs to page 1; displayed page numbers and figure locations were checked against rendered page images.
OCR degrades several symbols, especially epsilon, tau, theta, delta, derivatives, and fractions.
missing_sections: No experimental methods, material calibration, direct validation dataset, mechanics, electrochemistry, or uncertainty-quantification section is present.
low_confidence_equations: Core equations were manually checked against pages 2-4 and 12-13; the compact report omits some full anisotropic derivative and appendix expansion details.
visual_crop_limitations: Only full-page rendered views are available, so visual cards are page-level views rather than tightly cropped figures.
external_info_used: ScienceDirect was used to verify bibliographic metadata and the absence of an identified official artifact link on the record.
The official deal.II code gallery was used to document a later independent reimplementation, not author-provided code.

zh.one_sentence_summary: Kobayashi 将各向异性的非守恒相场与潜热扩散耦合，定性展示界面各向异性、无量纲潜热和界面局部噪声如何在无需显式追踪前沿的情况下重组枝晶尖端、侧枝、屏蔽竞争与尖角形成。

study_identity.domain: 纯物质熔体枝晶凝固的各向异性相场仿真
study_identity.evidence_mode: 自由能建模、尖锐界面渐近分析与二维定性参数研究

module_alignment.module_title: 微米级多孔碳中 CVD 沉积纳米硅
module_alignment.rationale: 论文不包含硅、多孔碳、化学气相沉积或电池电化学；只有通用弥散界面数值思想可借鉴。

module_alignment.module_title: 锂化硅相变、晶化与力学条件
module_alignment.rationale: 论文研究液—固晶化与界面各向异性，但没有力学场、含锂相或力学控制的晶化判据。

module_alignment.module_title: 分相材料的相场—力学—电化学仿真
module_alignment.rationale: 这是移动界面、自由能、各向异性和扩散耦合的基础相场案例，但输运场是温度而非电化学变量，也没有力学平衡与本构关系。

module_alignment.module_title: 多尺度仿真方法与案例
module_alignment.rationale: 尖锐界面极限连接了弥散界面与界面描述，但没有原子尺度参数化、逐级尺度传递、系统模型或实验闭环。

research_overview.one_sentence_conclusion: 一个最简的各向异性相场—温度模型可以定性再现多类枝晶形貌，但其定量可信度受弥散界面厚度及空间、时间分辨率限制。
research_overview.why_worth_reading: 这是一篇紧凑的奠基性案例，清楚展示自由能、角向界面各向异性、潜热耦合、尖锐界面解释、扰动与数值分辨率如何共同决定涌现的分枝形貌。
research_overview.research_problem: 研究要寻找一个定义在全域上的最小场模型，使其无需显式保存和移动界面，也能处理固液拓扑变化并生成真实感枝晶形貌。
research_overview.prior_gap: 显式移动边界方法在界面合并或脱离时需要复杂的界面管理，也难以推广到三维；单纯各向同性相场又不足以解释强定向枝晶。
research_overview.core_contribution: 论文建立了方向相关的 Allen–Cahn 型相场与焓形式热方程，渐近联系到各向异性曲率定律，并分析形貌随潜热、各向异性模态/强度和噪声的变化。
research_overview.scope_boundary: 模型针对热扩散率相同的单组分纯熔体，忽略流动、相变力学、溶质输运、电化学反应和定量收敛；其中类雪花图案也不代表气相生长雪晶。

research_system.research_object: 研究对象是纯单组分熔体在热驱动下凝固为晶体，固液界面可失稳形成胞状或枝晶形貌。
geometry_and_scale: 全部算例为二维，采用 9×9 方域或 12×3 长方形通道；弥散界面特征厚度由 ε 控制。
phases_and_composition: 序参量 p=0 表示液体，p=1 表示固体，中间陡峭过渡层就是界面；纯熔体模型没有组成场。
process_and_loading: 热过冷驱动凝固，热扩散搬运潜热，界面能平滑曲率，各向异性选择优先生长方向，小随机扰动触发侧枝。
state_variables: 求解变量是相场 p(r,t) 和无量纲温度 T(r,t)；界面方向 θ、法向速度 V、曲率 κ 和毛细函数 d₀(θ) 为派生量。
target_outputs: 目标输出包括界面形貌、枝晶尖端与侧枝演化、分枝竞争与屏蔽、尖角形成，以及它们对 K、δ、j 和噪声幅值的定性依赖。

model_and_mechanisms.framework: 模型将方向相关梯度能的非守恒 Ginzburg–Landau 相场与热扩散方程双向耦合：温度控制相变驱动力，相变速率释放潜热。
assumptions: 材料为纯熔体，唯一限制生长的体场是热扩散；忽略对流、Marangoni 流及相变膨胀或收缩。
固液热扩散率相同，体相稳定值固定为 p=0 和 p=1，使潜热只在界面经过时释放。
弥散界面应远薄于待解析形貌，随机项乘以 p(1−p)，因此主要作用于界面附近。
free_energy: Ginzburg–Landau 泛函由梯度惩罚和四次双阱势组成，双阱在液相 p=0 与固相 p=1 处稳定。
势阱深度差与 m 成正比，m 提供相的热力学偏好；ε 的方向依赖把界面能转化为各向异性毛细作用。

governing_equations.label: Ginzburg–Landau 自由能
governing_equations.explanation: 梯度项赋予界面有限能量与厚度，双阱稳定液体和固体，并通过 m 偏置相稳定性。

governing_equations.label: 各向异性相场演化
governing_equations.explanation: 变分松弛移动弥散界面；ε 的角向导数引入各向异性毛细效应，扩散项正则化界面，局部多项式控制相变和热驱动。

governing_equations.label: 潜热扩散
governing_equations.explanation: 温度扩散并只在 p 变化处获得热源；K 表示潜热相对于冷却强度的大小，把界面运动反馈给温度场。

governing_equations.label: 尖锐界面解释
governing_equations.explanation: 薄界面极限下，法向速度由热力学生长驱动力与方向相关毛细阻力 d₀κ 的竞争决定。

constitutive_relations.label: 温度相关驱动力
constitutive_relations.explanation: 过冷度增大固化驱动力，反正切函数同时保证 |m| 小于二分之一。

constitutive_relations.label: 角向各向异性
constitutive_relations.explanation: δ 控制各向异性强度，j 控制旋转模态，θ₀ 旋转优先生长方向。

coupling_logic: 温度通过 m(T) 控制相变；p 的变化通过 K∂ₜp 释放潜热并改变温度，从而形成热反馈闭环。
界面方向控制 ε 和毛细作用并选择分枝方向，曲率平滑小尺度结构，噪声则打破竞争侧枝间的对称性。

parameters.name: 方形计算域
parameters.role: 用于中心形核或壁面驱动凝固。

parameters.name: 长方形计算域
parameters.role: 用于定向凝固通道算例。

parameters.name: 方域网格
parameters.role: 方域算例的空间分辨率。

parameters.name: 通道网格
parameters.role: 通道算例的空间分辨率。

parameters.name: 平均界面厚度
parameters.role: 控制弥散界面厚度及其对尖锐前沿的逼近。

parameters.name: 相场松弛时间
parameters.role: 控制相场动力学响应和显式格式稳定性要求。

parameters.name: 驱动力饱和值
parameters.role: 限制温度相关相变驱动力的幅值。

parameters.name: 驱动力斜率
parameters.role: 控制 m(T) 在平衡温度附近的敏感度。

parameters.name: 噪声幅值
parameters.role: 为基准算例提供界面扰动。

parameters.name: 时间步
parameters.role: 相场显式更新与热场隐式更新所用时间离散。

initial_conditions: 算例包括由壁面冷却的平衡温度液体、带预设晶核的均匀过冷液体或受扰动的平面固液前沿；具体初态随图中算例变化。
boundary_conditions: 相场始终采用法向零通量；热边界按算例采用四壁冷却、仅左壁冷却其余绝热，或过冷凝固的全绝热边界。
numerical_implementation: 在均匀二维网格上用简单显式格式推进式 (3)，用简单隐式格式推进热方程，不使用专门的界面追踪。
均匀随机数 X∈[−1/2,1/2] 以 ap(1−p)X 进入，使扰动局部化于弥散界面。
reproducibility_check: 论文给出控制方程、主要参数、网格、时间步、边界条件类别和推进格式，因而可以重建代表性的定性算例。
缺少精确差分模板、线性求解器、终止条件、随机种子、每个图的完整初始晶核及原始代码；作者也明确说明界面速度未达到定量收敛。

key_results: 四重各向异性从 0 增至 0.050 时，形貌从各向同性指进逐渐转为强定向枝晶，分枝屏蔽和择优方向明显增强。
K 增大使平面或紧致前沿失稳，在研究区间内依次出现胞状、狭缝、尖端分裂和更细的分枝形貌。
在非振荡尖端条件下，噪声幅值显著改变侧枝选择；尖端振荡存在时，分枝对噪声较不敏感。
validation_and_comparison: 验证主要是定性的：模拟形貌类似常见枝晶，并再现平滑、失稳、择优方向、屏蔽和侧枝等预期现象。
尖锐界面渐近式为弥散方程与热力学驱动力/各向异性曲率之间提供理论一致性，但没有网格收敛的速度对比。
论文没有拟合具体材料实验，也没有比较实测尖端速度、分枝间距或温度历程。
mechanistic_interpretation: 各向异性毛细函数中的角向导数会放大很小的调制，从而选择分枝方向；当 d₀(θ) 变负时可形成尖角。
潜热降低局部过冷度，并通过温度场耦合相邻尖端，使其围绕散热能力发生竞争和屏蔽。
非振荡情形下噪声不控制主尖端速度，却会偏置年轻侧枝的存活；确定性尖端振荡则可成为更强的分枝来源。
sensitivity_and_uncovered: 研究改变 K、各向异性强度 δ、模态 j 与噪声幅值，但只覆盖很小的参数子集，也没有系统的收敛或不确定性分析。
未覆盖对流、机械应力与变形、溶质或电荷输运、电化学界面动力学、多相复合边界和气相生长晶面。
experimental_correspondence: 与实验的对应仅停留在形貌层面：模型生成视觉上合理的枝晶类别，但没有针对具体材料试样或测量场进行标定。
六重类雪花图案被作者明确限定为过冷水凝固，不能视为对气相雪晶生长的验证。

module_value: 对多孔碳中 CVD 纳米硅而言，论文只提供通用移动界面数值方法，不涉及沉积化学、孔结构、硅碳接触或电池性能。
对锂化硅相变力学而言，角向界面能可启发晶体各向异性建模，但锂热力学、应力、塑性与晶化判据都需另行加入。
对相场—力学—电化学而言，论文可作为序参量、双阱自由能、弥散界面、输运耦合、边界条件、各向异性、扰动和分辨率限制的清晰模板；热耦合必须替换或扩展为电化学与力学场。
对多尺度仿真而言，弥散到尖锐界面的渐近分析展示了一种跨描述连接，但没有自下而上的参数传递或系统级实验闭环。
reusable_elements: 可复用内容包括四次双阱、方向相关梯度系数、有界温度驱动力、潜热源、尖锐界面毛细解释、界面局部噪声和形貌参数研究。
作者关于界面宽度必须小于形貌尺度的明确警告，可直接转化为网格和模型分辨率验收准则。
limitations_and_next_steps: 面向电池时，应以浓度和电化学势替代单纯温度驱动，加入应力相关自由能与力学平衡，并在活性界面定义反应和通量条件。
在定量解释速度或分枝间距前，需要网格/时间收敛、薄界面修正、参数标定和直接实验观测量。
research_value_resources.reproducibility_verdict: 依据文中方程和设置可以较充分重建定性基准；deal.II 后续还提供了各向同性定向凝固子集的独立实现，但由于原始代码、随机种子、差分模板和完整算例文件缺失，无法精确复现 1993 年全部图像。

quick_read: p=0 与 p=1 分别表示液体和固体，有限厚度过渡层替代显式界面追踪。
相场为非守恒热驱动场，热方程中的 K∂ₜp 是局部化于界面的潜热源。
方向相关 ε 及其角向导数产生各向异性毛细作用与优先生长方向。
数值研究采用 300×300 或 400×100 网格的简单显式/隐式推进，重点是定性形貌而非收敛速度。
噪声偏置侧枝存活，但振荡尖端可通过更强、对噪声不敏感的机制产生侧枝。

argument_map.gap: 显式追踪界面在拓扑变化时很繁琐，而能生成真实枝晶的最简弥散模型仍需同时包含各向异性与热反馈。
argument_map.core_contribution: 各向异性相场方程与潜热扩散方程组成全域模型，能够生成多类枝晶形貌并具有尖锐界面解释。
argument_map.method_logic: 双阱区分液固相，梯度能正则化界面，温度偏置相变，潜热反馈温度，角向 ε 选择方向，局部噪声触发侧枝竞争。
decisive_evidence: 各向异性扫描系统地展示从指进到强定向枝晶的转变，而非只给出单张代表图。
噪声扫描区分主尖端传播与侧枝选择，并揭示振荡/非振荡两种分枝机制。
尖锐界面极限独立于形貌图解释热力学驱动力与各向异性曲率的作用。
limitations: 计算面向整晶定性形貌，空间和时间分辨率不足以精确给出界面速度。
最简纯熔体模型没有流动、力学、多组分输运或材料特定实验标定。
future_work: 定量使用需要更薄界面、更细时空网格、受限计算域和材料特定验证。
迁移到电池分相需要加入电化学输运、反应边界和力学。

central_claims.claim: 最简各向异性弥散界面模型无需显式追踪界面即可生成多类枝晶。
central_claims.evidence_summary: 同一组耦合方程随 K 和各向异性变化产生紧致、胞状、尖端分裂和定向枝晶形貌。
central_claims.what_it_proves: 在所测算例范围内，模型机制足以定性生成形貌。
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: 它不能证明对具体材料的定量预测精度或收敛界面速度。
central_claims.open_question: 定量预测需要哪些薄界面修正和标定参数？

central_claims.claim: 很小的各向异性即可控制宏观分枝方向和尖角形成。
central_claims.evidence_summary: 图 7 在 δ=0–0.050 内出现显著形貌变化，毛细函数则解释角向导数的放大作用。
central_claims.what_it_proves: 在模型区间内，角向界面能是主要形貌选择因素。
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: 所选余弦各向异性没有针对具体晶体实测界面能标定。
central_claims.open_question: 电池材料的 σ(θ) 应如何从原子计算或实验获得？

central_claims.claim: 当确定性尖端振荡不存在时，噪声主要控制侧枝选择。
central_claims.evidence_summary: 一种区间中噪声改变侧枝区而不改变主尖端速度；振荡尖端对噪声变化较不敏感。
central_claims.what_it_proves: 不同分枝区间可具有不同扰动敏感度。
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: 人为均匀随机项不是实测物理涨落谱。
central_claims.open_question: 复合电极中哪些真实非均匀性应替代任意噪声？

pipeline: 为壁面冷却、定向生长或过冷熔体晶核设置 p 和 T 初态。
计算方向相关 ε、有界热驱动力 m(T) 和界面局部随机扰动。
显式推进各向异性相场，隐式推进潜热方程，并施加相场零通量和算例特定热边界。
比较 K、δ、j 与噪声幅值下的界面形貌，并借助尖锐界面毛细定律解释。
method_understanding.algorithm_pseudocode:
初始化 p、T、几何、边界和参数。
每个时间步计算方向与 m(T)，加入界面局部噪声，显式更新 p，再用潜热隐式更新 T。
保存 p 等值线并比较不同参数算例。

algorithm_steps.action: 为选定凝固算例初始化相场与温度场。
algorithm_steps.inputs: 计算域、网格、晶核或平面前沿、初始温度、边界条件
algorithm_steps.outputs: t=0 时的 p 和 T

algorithm_steps.action: 计算各向异性、热驱动力和界面局部扰动。
显式推进相场并隐式推进温度场。
algorithm_steps.outputs: 更新后的 p 与 T

algorithm_steps.action: 记录相场等值线并定性比较分枝形貌和速度。

method_understanding.engineering_derivation_sketch: 从双阱自由能和梯度代价出发，以梯度流推进 p，并令梯度系数依赖界面法向。把 m 与过冷度相连，再以 K∂ₜp 作为热方程源项满足焓守恒。沿薄界面法向拉伸坐标，可得到由过冷驱动并受各向异性曲率抵抗的法向速度定律。
implementation_details: 均匀网格为 300×300 或 400×100，时间步 0.0002；相场显式、热扩散隐式。
不使用专门前沿追踪；检查到的来源中没有原始实现代码和随机种子。

datasets: 没有发布数据集；评价对象是不同热参数、各向异性和噪声条件下生成的相场等值线序列。
metrics: 论文主要定性评价界面稳定性、胞状结构、尖端分裂、分枝方向、屏蔽、尖角、侧枝区域及近似尖端速度行为。
main_results: 各向异性和潜热系统地重组全局枝晶形貌，噪声则主要在非振荡区间选择侧枝。
ablation_or_comparison_takeaways: 各向同性到各向异性的扫描隔离了角向界面能的形貌选择作用；噪声幅值扫描区分随机选择与振荡分枝。

numeric_results.interpretation: 很小的角向调制就足以使解进入定性不同的分枝区间。
numeric_results.what_it_does_not_prove: 该扫描不能给出普适最优各向异性或真实材料标定值。

numeric_results.interpretation: 这是定性形貌计算采用的时间更新间隔。
numeric_results.what_it_does_not_prove: 论文明确没有证明时间步收敛或精确界面速度。

theory_understanding.problem_formulation: 用两个全域光滑场逼近各向异性、热驱动的尖锐固液边界，同时保留热力学驱动、毛细平滑、潜热、拓扑变化和择优晶向。

key_equations.label: 相场与热场耦合演化
key_equations.explanation: 相场方程移动并塑造界面；热方程输运和返回潜热，温度再通过 m(T) 闭合反馈。

key_equations.label: 薄界面速度定律
key_equations.explanation: 法向速度由热力学生长驱动力与各向异性毛细曲率惩罚竞争决定。

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: 把自由能变分转化为相场运动。
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: 除热驱动促使固化外，界面沿降低弥散自由能的方向运动。

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: 把相变与潜热释放耦合。
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: 液体转为固体的位置释放潜热，局部温度升高并削弱剩余过冷度。

theorem_or_principle_chain.role: 把全域相场方程连接到移动边界曲率定律。
theorem_or_principle_chain.intuition: 足够薄的弥散层表现为具有方向相关界面张力和迁移率的前沿。

assumptions: 纯熔体热扩散是唯一限速体场，且两相扩散率相同。
被解析结构应宽于相场层，网格需要足够细以抑制计算晶格各向异性。
key_results: 各向异性弥散模型可再现多类枝晶，并具有包含驱动力、表面张力和各向异性的尖锐界面解释。
theory_understanding.engineering_proof_sketch: 令界面厚度趋于零，引入沿界面法向的拉伸坐标并假设行波剖面，求解相应非线性特征值问题；最低阶平衡给出驱动力减各向异性毛细曲率的速度关系。
limitations: 若界面相对形貌过厚，或网格/时间步不足以收敛速度，渐近联系也不能弥补离散误差。

task_context: 应用是壁冷、定向凝固和过冷熔体形核的二维定性形貌预测。
experimental_setup: 没有实验室实验；数值算例改变潜热、各向异性与扰动幅值并比较相场等值线序列。
constraints: 结果受无量纲参数、均匀网格、简化热物理和弥散界面分辨率约束。
transfer_limits: 电池应用必须加入电化学自由能、守恒物种输运、反应动力学、复合几何与力学，不能直接定量迁移形貌趋势。

code.evidence: 1993 年论文记录没有作者代码链接，但 deal.II 官方代码库提供了基于该模型的各向同性定向凝固子集独立实现。
code.notes: deal.II 示例是后续可复现派生基准，不是原始仿真源码。

data.evidence: 论文报告生成的形貌图而非发布数据集，官方记录没有数据存档。
data.notes: 只能近似数字化图像，未核实到原始场数据。

models.evidence: 数学模型在论文中完整描述，但未核实到原始可执行模型或算例归档。
models.notes: deal.II 独立实现只覆盖一个子集，已列在代码资源中。

parser_limitations: 扫描版双栏 PDF 的解析器把多数段落页码标为第 1 页；显示页码和图位置已依据页面渲染核对。
OCR 对 ε、τ、θ、δ、导数和分式等符号存在明显损坏。
missing_sections: 没有实验方法、材料标定、直接验证数据集、力学、电化学或不确定性量化部分。
low_confidence_equations: 核心方程已人工对照第 2–4、12–13 页；紧凑报告省略了部分完整角向导数和附录展开。
visual_crop_limitations: 当前只有整页渲染，因此图卡是页面级视图而非紧裁剪图。
external_info_used: ScienceDirect 用于核实书目信息及论文记录中没有官方制品链接。
deal.II 官方代码库用于记录后续独立复现，而非作者代码。
